clinic.title: Clinic waiting times
clinic.order: Chronological: visit_id runs week by week, Monday to Friday, slot 1 to 20 within each day.
clinic.order_meaning: Row order is time order. Neighbouring rows are neighbouring appointments.
clinic.scenario: A clinic manager wants to know the average time patients wait past their appointment time over the last 100 weeks, without reviewing every record.
clinic.population: All 10,000 appointments in this file (100 weeks x 5 days x 20 slots). It is not every clinic or every week.
clinic.provenance: Newly simulated for this activity by data-prep/prepare_data.py (seed 20261105). It follows the layout of the course notebook's clinic_visits.csv, which was not available, so its values are NOT the notebook's values.
clinic.license: Created for this activity; reuse with the rest of this repository.

columns.name: slot
columns.meaning: Appointment slot within the day, 1 (first) to 20 (last)

columns.name: wait_time
columns.meaning: Minutes the patient waited after the appointment time

costs.title: Healthcare costs
costs.order: The order of the source file. row_id is added; the order has no documented meaning and is not a time sequence.
costs.order_meaning: Row order is file order only. It is not a time sequence.
costs.scenario: A health-plan analyst wants to estimate average medical charges per person in this list without reviewing every record.
costs.population: The 1,338 people in this file. It is a teaching dataset, not a representative sample of current claims.
costs.provenance: The insurance.csv teaching dataset distributed with Brett Lantz's book Machine Learning with R (Packt), as mirrored in the stedy/Machine-Learning-with-R-datasets GitHub repository. The book describes it as hypothetical (simulated) data created using US Census Bureau demographic statistics; the repository itself documents nothing further, and how charges were generated is not published. Unchanged except for the added row_id and age_band columns.
costs.license: No licence is stated in the source repository. Widely redistributed for teaching; confirm this use fits your course policy.

columns.name: row_id
columns.meaning: Row number in the source file, 1-1,338 (added)

heart.title: Wearable heart rate
heart.order: Chronological by timestamp. Minutes with no reading are absent, so consecutive rows are not always one minute apart.
heart.order_meaning: Row order is time order, but with gaps: row number is not the same as time.
heart.scenario: A researcher wants to estimate one wearer's average heart rate over a week from a subset of the recorded minutes.
heart.population: The recorded minutes of one wearer's week (25 April - 1 May 2016). It is not every minute of that week, and not other people.
heart.provenance: A real extract from the Crowd-sourced Fitbit datasets (Furberg, Brinton, Keating & Ortiz, Zenodo 2016): participant 5577150313, 2016-04-25 00:00 to 2016-05-01 23:59 (device local time), export 4.12.16-5.12.16. heart_rate_bpm is the mean of that minute's readings (the device records every few seconds). activity_state is derived from the same participant's Fitbit sleep log (asleep or restless = sleep) and minute intensity (fairly or very active = exercise); everything else is rest. These are device estimates, not observed or clinically verified labels.
heart.license: CC BY 4.0. Cite: Furberg R, Brinton J, Keating M, Ortiz A. Crowd-sourced Fitbit datasets 03.12.2016-05.12.2016. Zenodo; 2016. doi:10.5281/zenodo.53894

columns.name: row_id
columns.meaning: Row number, 1 to N, in time order

columns.name: timestamp
columns.meaning: Start of the minute, device local time

columns.name: heart_rate_bpm
columns.meaning: Mean of the heart-rate readings in that minute

columns.name: n_readings
columns.meaning: How many device readings were averaged for that minute

columns.name: activity_state
columns.meaning: Device-derived state: sleep, rest or exercise (see provenance)
